label: early original-phase u/s/t/p input (esp. u at t=3) after e/j/z/c/b/w/v/a prefix
explanation: Fires almost only in the original phase (95% of mass), at t=0 and t=2..4 (t=3 alone holds 58% of mass). It never fires at t=1, at t>=6, or at the delimiter, and rarely in the copy phase (a little at recall_idx=1). The input token is the main driver: u (15x lift, 38% of mass), then s, t, p. Input u at t=0 always fires, but weakly (7% of mass). At t=2..4, whether it fires and how strongly depends on the prefix. The largest activations (u or s at t=3) come after prefixes of e/j/z/c/b/w/v/a, especially when the sequence starts with e. It fires much less often on repeated tokens (in_first=0). Many u/s/t/p inputs at these positions stay inactive, so prefix dependence that the predicate does not capture limits precision. Dev F1 is 0.505 with mass recall 0.76. A stricter prefix condition reaches F1 0.575 but only 0.51 mass recall.
